It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former rank was {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}. {{nihongo|'''Yoshimiko Shrine'''|吉御子神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

== Overview ==
According to shrine tradition, a divine descent occurred in year 68 of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}, and in year 2 of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}, Yoshihiko-no-Mikoto and Yoshihime-no-Mikoto, children of Ukahiko, were enshrined before Tanikuro-no-Mimae; this is said to be the founding. It corresponds to the western shrine among the division of the shrine to east and west due to disaster in {{ill|811|Q29946|qid=Q29946}} (Kōnin 2)<ref name="JAPAN-GEOGRAPHIC.TV">[https://japan-geographic.tv/shiga/konan-yoshimikojinja.html Yoshimiko Shrine, Konan City, Shiga JAPAN-GEOGRAPHIC.TV] accessed 2013-05-01</ref>. The current honden was moved from the former honden of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamigamo Shrine}} in Kyoto in 1865 (Keiō 1), after shrine buildings were badly damaged in {{ill|1864|Q7704|qid=Q7704}} (Genji 1), and was designated a national {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}} in {{ill|1921|ab|1921|af|1921|als|1921|am|1921 == Festivals ==

* Annual festival: May 1
: * It has a paired relationship with {{ill|Yoshihime Shrine|Q11412752|qid=Q11412752}}, and mikoshi from both shrines come out on that day. This is called the "Ishibe Grand Festival."

== Cultural properties ==
; Important Cultural Property (National designation)
* Honden - former honden of Kamigamo Shrine in Kyoto (early Edo period architecture, moved in 1865), three-bay nagare-zukuri, cypress-bark roof, designated April 30, 1921
* Wooden seated Yoshihiko-no-Mikoto statue (with two wooden seated attendant deity statues) - Heian period, wood

; City designated cultural property
* Mikoshi
